speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis symptoms, and do you have a known history of smoking or environmental exposure to dust and chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the 11-year duration and copious purulent sputum are significant. As a non-smoker with this specific history, have you ever been exposed to dust mites, mold, or bird droppings, and do you have any history of nasal polyps or asthma?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential and Total IgE level.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA). The clinical presentation of chronic productive cough, recurrent "bronchitis," and copious purulent sputum in a non-smoker, despite a misdiagnosis of pyelonephritis, is highly suggestive of ABPA. Please request images of the chest CT to confirm central bronchiectasis and mucus plugging.
